title: 5 Sana Alternatives for Enterprise Knowledge and AI Agents
summary: Sana alternatives compared across deployment, knowledge structure, and auditability: Jinba Brain, Glean, Guru, Notion AI, and Docebo/LearnUpon, rated for regulated enterprise AI agents.
body_markdown:
### Summary


- Sana is a capable AI-native learning and knowledge platform, but it is cloud-only and offers no per-answer audit trail, a blocker for banks, insurers, and other regulated enterprises deploying AI agents.
- RAG-based platforms like Sana return answers that shift as the underlying document corpus changes; ontology-validated knowledge records return the same validated answer every time.
- This guide compares five alternatives across deployment model, knowledge structure, and auditability: Jinba Brain, Glean, Guru, Notion AI, and the LMS category (Docebo and LearnUpon).
- Action item: confirm whether the organization needs formal employee training (an LMS) or governed knowledge for AI agents (a knowledge layer) before shortlisting vendors; Sana sells into both categories.
- For regulated enterprises that require on-premise or air-gapped deployment, FIBO/ACORD-validated records, and SHA-256 source traceability,[Jinba](https://jinba.io/) is purpose-built, with pilots typically running 4–8 weeks.


Sana is recognized for its AI-native design, fast onboarding, and support for[over 50 languages](https://sanalabs.com/products/sana/pricing) . For many L&D and knowledge teams, it is a meaningful step up from legacy systems like Workday Learning. Enterprise buyers in regulated industries face a different set of questions: Can internal data stay on-premises? Can an AI agent's answer be traced to a specific, version-controlled source record? Will the same critical question always return the same correct answer?


Sana was not built to address these requirements. This article maps five sana alternatives across the dimensions where those gaps matter most: deployment model, knowledge structure, and auditability.


---


## What Sana Does Well, and Where It Stops Short


Sana ships as two distinct products. Sana Learn is an AI-powered Learning Experience Platform competing with traditional LMS tools. Sana Agents is its enterprise knowledge and AI agent layer. Both run on a cloud-hosted architecture, and both are relevant to different buyer searches.


For cloud-first companies with general-purpose knowledge and training needs, Sana is a capable platform. Its limitations become apparent when regulated enterprises apply their specific requirements.


[Sana's pricing page](https://sanalabs.com/products/sana/pricing) confirms single-tenant cloud as the enterprise deployment option. On-premises or air-gapped hosting is not offered. For banks and insurers whose internal data cannot reside in a third-party cloud, this is a structural constraint rather than a configuration preference.


Security credentials are platform-level: SOC 2 and ISO 27001, plus permission mirroring. This satisfies general cloud security reviews but does not provide the per-answer audit trail that regulators and risk functions require. There is no mechanism to trace a specific AI-generated answer back to a version-controlled fact record.


Answer consistency carries a similar limitation. Systems that retrieve relevant text chunks at query time produce answers that vary depending on which chunks surface. For a question about credit policy, claims handling, or compliance classification, that variability constitutes a compliance risk rather than an acceptable tolerance.

## A Closer Look at Each Alternative


### 1. Jinba Brain: Ontology-Validated Knowledge for Regulated AI Agents


[Jinba Brain](https://jinba.io/) is not a RAG-based knowledge tool. It is a specialized knowledge layer that makes company data answerable, not merely findable. Where general-purpose data platforms index content for retrieval, Jinba Brain stores company knowledge as ontology-defined, schema-validated, linked records. Business rules are encoded in the structure of the data itself; they are not inferred at query time by a large language model.


The practical consequence is consistency. For credit exposure limits in banking, a RAG-based system retrieves whichever text chunks score highest at query time, and the answer changes as the document corpus shifts. Jinba Brain encodes those limits in a schema built on the Financial Industry Business Ontology (FIBO) for banking and finance, and the ACORD Information Model for insurance. Every AI agent answers from the same validated record, every time.


Auditability is structural. Every fact record stores its source path and a SHA-256 hash. Raw data is never modified. The pipeline reads it on a schedule, extracts facts using a fine-tuned small model rather than a large general-purpose LLM, and passes each candidate fact through an Evaluator that checks schema conformance, referenced IDs, deduplication, and hash integrity before a human reviewer approves it. Nothing enters the knowledge base automatically.


A second learning loop captures user corrections. When an agent gives a wrong answer and a user corrects it, that correction updates a Skill: a reusable procedure or decision criterion. Human review is a mandatory gate on this loop too. In regulated industries, a single incorrect fact propagating to every deployed agent is a compliance event. The governance architecture reflects that.


[Jinba](https://jinba.io/) supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment, which is a prerequisite for banks and insurers whose data cannot leave their environment. The platform carries SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance, and its deterministic, rule-based execution runs 15 to 60 times cheaper than stochastic AI agents at scale.


The recommended buying process is a 4 to 8 week pilot within one department. Accuracy is measured on the client's own questions, not generic benchmarks, with a data scientist owning the evaluation dataset. Jinba AI Consulting has approximately[70 enterprise case studies](https://jinba.io/) , including work with MUFG/Mitsubishi Bank. Pricing is quote-based.


---


### 2. Glean: Enterprise-Wide Search Across Applications


Glean connects to hundreds of workplace applications and surfaces relevant content through a unified search interface. Its core purpose is making existing company information findable across silos, and it handles that well at scale.


Glean uses a RAG-based approach, which means its strength is discovery and synthesis of unstructured content. It does not structure that content into validated records, and it does not guarantee consistent answers for automated agents working from business rules.


On deployment, Glean has historically been a cloud product. A[partnership with Dell](https://www.dell.com/en-us/blog/dell-glean-on-premises-solution-enterprise-ai-search/) has introduced an on-premises option, which opens the door for enterprises with stricter data residency requirements.


Glean is best suited to organizations whose primary need is intelligent search across cloud applications. It is not purpose-built for the auditability and schema governance that regulated AI agent deployments require.


---


### 3. Guru: Knowledge Embedded in Daily Workflows


Guru is built for sales, support, and customer-facing teams. Its browser extension surfaces relevant knowledge cards directly inside the tools those teams already use: Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, and Chrome. For capturing and distributing tactical knowledge like support macros, product FAQs, and sales playbooks, it is a market leader in its category.


The knowledge model is unstructured. Cards are authored and maintained by humans, and the platform tracks content history rather than providing record-level auditability. Guru is cloud-only, with no on-premise option.


For compliance functions, risk teams, or AI agents that need to answer policy questions with verifiable precision, Guru's model is not designed to meet that bar. It is the right tool for workflow-embedded knowledge distribution to revenue teams.


---


### 4. Notion AI: AI Assistance Within the Notion Workspace


Notion AI extends the Notion platform with drafting, summarization, and Q&A capabilities across a team's existing pages and databases. For teams that already use Notion as their central wiki and project management environment, the integration is frictionless.


The scope is limited to content inside Notion. Notion AI does not connect to external enterprise systems, cannot enforce schema or governance rules, and has no deployment option outside Notion's cloud. It is a reasonable choice for teams that need lightweight AI assistance on documentation they already manage in Notion, and a poor fit for enterprise-wide knowledge governance.


---


### 5. The LMS Category: Docebo and LearnUpon


If the search for a Sana alternative is rooted in formal employee training, compliance modules, and course completion tracking rather than AI agent knowledge, the relevant category is the Learning Management System. Docebo and LearnUpon are established platforms in this space, each offering structured course delivery, certification tracking, and compliance reporting at enterprise scale.


This article's focus is on enterprise knowledge for AI agents rather than the LMS category. Sana Learn competes in the LMS and LXP market; Sana Agents competes in the knowledge layer market. Buyers should confirm which problem they are solving before selecting a vendor.


## How to Choose


The decision narrows quickly once the deployment and governance requirements are fixed.


- Regulated industries requiring on-premise or air-gapped deployment, record-level auditability, and consistent answers for AI agents: Jinba Brain is purpose-built for this. No other platform on this list encodes business rules in validated schemas, stores every fact with a SHA-256 hash, or gates every knowledge update behind human approval.
- Enterprise-wide search and content discovery across cloud applications: Glean is the strongest option, with an on-premise configuration now available through Dell for teams with data residency constraints.
- **Sales and support teams needing knowledge surfaced inside CRMs and communication tools:** Guru leads this category.
- Teams already using Notion who need an AI assistant for documentation and summarization: Notion AI is the natural, low-friction choice.
- **Formal training, compliance courses, and certification management:** Evaluate Docebo or LearnUpon rather than any platform on this list.


---


## The Distinction That Matters


Most sana alternative searches start with features: can a platform connect to existing tools, does it support the languages an organization uses, what does it cost. Those are necessary questions. For regulated enterprises deploying AI agents to answer policy, compliance, or risk questions, the foundational question is different: is the system's knowledge verifiable?


RAG-based platforms make data findable. Jinba Brain makes it answerable: every fact validated against an industry-standard schema, every record traceable to its source, every knowledge update approved by a human before it reaches any agent.


That distinction is what separates a knowledge layer built for regulated deployment from a search tool built for general-purpose discovery. Sana and most of its competitors sit firmly in the second category.


If your AI agents need to give consistent, auditable answers from internal company data,[request a free assessment from Jinba](https://jinba.io/consulting) to see what a verified knowledge base looks like on your own data.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best Sana alternative for regulated industries?


Jinba Brain is the strongest Sana alternative when on-premise or air-gapped deployment, record-level auditability, and consistent AI-agent answers are non-negotiable. Unlike cloud-only platforms, Jinba Brain stores knowledge as ontology-validated records with source paths and SHA-256 hashes, and requires human approval before updates reach agents. That makes it suitable for banks, insurers, and other regulated enterprises. If the priority is enterprise search rather than governed knowledge, Glean may be a better fit.


### Is Sana available on-premise or air-gapped?


No. Sana offers single-tenant cloud as its enterprise deployment option, according to its pricing page, but does not provide on-premises or air-gapped hosting. This matters for banks and insurers whose internal data cannot reside in a third-party cloud. Buyers with strict data residency requirements should shortlist vendors such as Jinba Brain, which supports on-premise, air-gapped, and private cloud deployment.


### What is the difference between Sana Learn and Sana Agents?


Sana Learn is an AI-powered learning experience platform for employee training, while Sana Agents is an enterprise knowledge and AI-agent layer. Sana Learn competes with LMS and LXP platforms; Sana Agents competes with knowledge platforms. Buyers should confirm whether they need formal course delivery and completion tracking or governed knowledge for AI agents, because those are different purchase categories.


### How does Jinba Brain differ from RAG-based platforms like Sana?


Jinba Brain uses ontology-validated knowledge records instead of query-time RAG retrieval. That means business rules and facts are encoded in schemas such as FIBO for finance and ACORD for insurance, rather than inferred from whichever text chunks surface. The result is consistent answers from the same validated record every time, with a source path and SHA-256 hash for auditability. RAG platforms are strong for discovery and synthesis but can return variable answers as the underlying corpus changes.


### Can Sana provide record-level audit trails for AI-generated answers?


Sana provides platform-level security credentials such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001, plus permission mirroring, but it does not provide a per-answer audit trail back to a version-controlled fact record. For regulated risk and compliance teams, platform certification is not the same as record-level traceability. A system like Jinba Brain is designed to trace each fact to its source path and hash, with human approval gating every knowledge update.


### Which Sana alternative is best for enterprise-wide search?


Glean is the strongest option for enterprise-wide search and content discovery across cloud applications. It connects to hundreds of workplace tools and uses RAG to surface relevant content. Glean has historically been cloud-only, though a Dell partnership has introduced an on-premises option. It is less suited to schema-governed AI-agent answers than a purpose-built knowledge layer.


### How long does it take to implement Jinba Brain as a Sana alternative?


A typical Jinba Brain pilot runs 4 to 8 weeks within one department. The process measures accuracy on the client's own questions rather than generic benchmarks, with a data scientist owning the evaluation dataset. That scope lets regulated buyers validate deployment, governance, and answer quality before expanding. Implementation timelines beyond the pilot depend on the number of knowledge domains and integration requirements.


### How much does a Sana alternative like Jinba Brain cost?


Jinba Brain pricing is quote-based, so there is no public list price to compare directly with Sana's published plans. The business case should account for deployment model, governance requirements, and total cost of ownership. Jinba's deterministic, rule-based execution is positioned as 15 to 60 times cheaper than stochastic AI agents at scale. For a like-for-like comparison, ask vendors to price the same pilot scope and user population.


### Is Guru or Notion AI a good Sana alternative?


Guru and Notion AI are good Sana alternatives only for narrower use cases. Guru excels at surfacing knowledge cards inside sales and support workflows such as Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, and Chrome, but it is cloud-only and uses unstructured cards. Notion AI is a low-friction assistant for teams already working inside Notion, but it is limited to Notion content and offers no external enterprise system coverage or schema governance. Neither is built for regulated AI-agent knowledge governance.


### Should I choose an LMS or a knowledge layer as a Sana alternative?


Choose an LMS if your primary need is formal employee training, compliance courses, certification tracking, and course completion reporting; Docebo and LearnUpon are relevant options. Choose a knowledge layer if your priority is consistent, auditable answers from internal company data for AI agents; Jinba Brain is purpose-built for that. Sana spans both categories through Sana Learn and Sana Agents, so buyers should define the problem before comparing vendors.
